prompt_en: A photographic space-horror scene records a dangerous moment aboard a spacecraft. At the right side of a wide rectangular hatch, a woman whose facial appearance and hairstyle follow the supplied portrait crouches beside the final clamp of a temporary clear pressure partition. Her dark chin-length bob and wispy fringe frame large brown eyes, softly rounded cheeks and natural pink lips. Her concentrated face carries an intimate, vulnerable presence within the emergency; a small sheen of perspiration catches the work light. She wears a fitted off-white thermal coverall with worn utility seams. The corridor around her still holds breathable air. Beyond the transparent partition, two frost-coated cryogenic storage capsules flank a torn opening in the ship's outer wall, exposing small sharp stars in black space. The partition is the thin physical boundary preserving the corridor. Its upper and side edges are already captured by evenly spaced metal clamps; its clear sheet bows away from her into the depressurized bay. At the lower-right corner, a short unfinished seam remains visibly open just to the left of a red over-center lever. Fine white condensation threads stream through that gap away from the corridor toward the open bay. She has one knee on the corridor floor and the opposite boot planted firmly beside her. Her right hand closes around the red lever, folding it toward the lower-right jamb; her left palm braces the same solid jamb above the clamp. Her arms remain on the corridor side of the sheet. She watches the remaining gap as she works, lips slightly parted, with the incompletely closed lever and the escaping threads visible together. Photograph from the corridor at a shallow oblique angle, wide enough to include all four partition edges, her face, both connected arms, the grounded knee and boot, and the torn hull beyond. Keep the clamp large and unobstructed beside her hand. A warm portable work lamp describes her face and fingers against cold blue reflections on the transparent sheet; a dim red service beacon recedes into the bay. The vulnerable clear surface, purposeful hand, and indifferent patch of outer space form the photograph's visual hierarchy, with tactile condensation and restrained documentary grain.

adult_appeal_brief.contextual_comparison: The contextual inventory is empty, so no axis candidate is invented. At the same subtle supporting strength, A1 tears/closed lips would shift attention toward a prescribed fear demonstration; the baseline preserves vulnerable purposeful concentration and its face-hand-gap relationship.

h_f2_material_decisions.rationale: R00, composition-comparison.md: The complete bundle needs a bust crop, an existing centered vertical background element, one narrow rear luminous aperture and darker front surfaces. No such existing aperture/background owner is independently frozen; native approval is false. A bust crop would also trade away the hand-to-gap-to-hull continuity. No whole-cue realization is admitted; baseline keeps its warm front work light.

R01, composition-comparison.md: The exact cue pools tears on lower eyelid margins and closes the lip seam. Alternative A1 realizes both on the same face while retaining the pressure work. A1 makes the fear explicit but reduces the baseline parted-lip concentration and adds a fine facial detail competing with the fine seal detail. Baseline chosen; no tear cue retained.

R02, composition-comparison.md: The complete source requires a porous paper/cloth carrier with fibers crossing wet/dry regions and a damp front fed by liquid contact. The pressure membrane is a clear nonporous sheet and the escaping material is airborne condensation. Calling that a capillary front would lose the actual material and contact relation. No such cue retained.

R03, composition-comparison.md: The source requires the body, low enclosing ceiling and one narrow exit to be visible with actual clearance. It explicitly describes an adult body; the frozen reference is appearance-only and supplies no adult fact. No whole-source authority is supplied. Its spatial compression cannot be treated as a mere face crop, and no compression is retained.

R04, composition-comparison.md: The source changes main-subject hair.style and hair.style.flyaway with same-hair ownership. Facial appearance and hairstyle are the one protected reference property, and there is no independently frozen hair-part owner graph qualifying this source. The final keeps the source portrait bob/fringe, adding no flyaway prescription.

R05, composition-comparison.md: This is a continuous liquid column from a visible outlet into a coherent receiving region, with water-column contact. A condensation thread through a pressure gap is not that liquid jet, and the vacuum bay is not a liquid receiving surface. No water jet is introduced.

R06, composition-comparison.md: The source is a shore-water flow corridor between breaking waves, with surface foam/sediment aligned seaward; it requires marine/aquatic primary context. The frozen spacecraft has neither waves nor shore water. Using its word corridor for the spacecraft would erase source meaning. No use.

R07, composition-comparison.md: The whole tactile cue needs a bent free flap still joined at a peel front, retained front texture, a thin edge, differently lit reverse, and exposed substrate. A2 realizes these at the same lower membrane corner. Its extra exposed gasket and reverse surface explain delamination but compete with the simple last clamp and create a second failure mechanism. Baseline chosen; no peeling flap retained.

R08, composition-comparison.md: The source stages a depicted camera and sitter opposite one another across a gap in a side view. The frozen capture camera is an unprescribed recording viewpoint, not a depicted device, and no second camera/sitter relationship is frozen. A clear pressure boundary cannot supply that missing camera owner. No use.

R09, composition-comparison.md: The source presses a person near a doorway and directs attention down a corridor from shadow. A3 retains the pressure work while turning her attention into the corridor and putting her near side in shadow. It gives suspense beyond the leak but weakens the face-gap-clamp attention line and the reference face readability. Baseline chosen; no corridor-watch cue retained.

R10, composition-comparison.md: The complete lateral-breast/bodice relation requires human and adult context plus a bounded outer contour distinguishable from arm/back. The frozen portrait establishes no adulthood and the source has no native approval. It is unrelated to the current survival boundary and cannot be reduced to a generic garment edge. No use.

R11, composition-comparison.md: The complete cue lowers a mask to reveal an unusually extended mouth on the same adult fictional face. That alters the protected portrait facial appearance and additionally needs adult context not frozen here. A space-horror label cannot authorize that facial mutation. No use.

R12, composition-comparison.md: The complete riverbank/shawl/hand-covering-face realization requires adult context and declares subject among its effects. It relocates the human into a specific folk-horror scene, and the covered face would obstruct the appearance comparison. No whole-source admission; no river/shawl motif retained.

R13, composition-comparison.md: The source makes folded organ-like tissue the outer silhouette of a fictional creature, not an organ prop beside a person. No existing creature is independently declared, and the subject is the reference-guided woman. A new creature cannot be silently supplied by a horror label. No use.

R14, composition-comparison.md: The complete transparent-partition cue includes a food tray resting in its transfer hatch and an adult attendant outside. It declares subject and broad effects on all four owners and has no native qualification. The independently chosen pressure membrane is not a food-transfer hatch; borrowing only transparent partition would discard the tray/hatch/attendant relation. No use.

R15, composition-comparison.md: The profile requires a clearly adult subject and deliberate eye-and-nose occlusion with a scene-bound contact, unfinished task and setting. The reference supplies no adult fact, and hiding that identity-bearing region would make the requested face comparison unobservable. No selected profile or occlusion duty is created.

R16, composition-comparison.md: The source contrasts a readable adult and clothing against repeated labyrinth-set boundaries; it warns against inferring actual captivity. No adult fact or repeated labyrinth construction is independently frozen. The current single pressure boundary is not a maze. No use.

R17, composition-comparison.md: The entire cue is two printed images of the same room with different depicted door counts, placed side by side. Its effects include subject and recording/relationship roles. Those print owners are not frozen and cannot replace the reference-guided subject; adding an evidentiary desk would shift the photograph to records rather than the current emergency. No use.

R18, composition-comparison.md: The full horror-comedy cue requires an adult calmly labeling a monstrous prop that dominates the same workstation. The present emergency has no monstrous prop or labeling task and no frozen adult fact. Ordinary purposeful labor alone cannot stand in for the complete contrast. No use.

R19, composition-comparison.md: The source only names concept object photography; it supplies no concrete owner/geometry or source condition that would improve this person-centered emergency. Turning the image into an object study would demote its reference-guided human subject without an admitted source realization. No source-specific visual effect retained.

R20, composition-comparison.md: The source requires surveillance or reflection context, rather than any clear surface. The membrane transmits the bay view and is not a surveillance mirror; no independent surveillance relationship is declared. No reflection capture cue retained.

R21, composition-comparison.md: The complete underwater figure/water-surface/distant-pool-ladder realization changes subject and many physical dimensions. It cannot use a spacecraft bay as a pool or equate vacuum risk with drowning, and it does not establish death. No source admission or borrowed water imagery.

R22, composition-comparison.md: The source is two rolled hair masses, each continuous with gathered scalp hair. Replacing the supplied short bob/fringe with space buns changes the protected hairstyle. The word space is an incidental homonym, not spacecraft meaning. No use.

Generic blue reflections already belong to the independent membrane, so no glossy outfit is borrowed.

The current sheet is intentionally unfinished and no internal anomaly is selected. Source effects are empty and it grants no profile selection authority here. The baseline independently carries an external boundary but does not adopt this full profile.

No such instrument correspondence is frozen. Adding it would create a second, large explanatory comparison unrelated to closing the seal; source authority remains false. The source reference-guided subject is on the habitable side with visible face; outside suit staging is not admitted through this source. No EVA/tether cue retained.

Neither book nor that support setup is frozen; both hands currently perform pressure work. No book-face cue retained.

A bowed plastic pressure membrane is not that lens/plate pair. No Newton-ring effect is added.
